# The possibility of having unified refund/compensation guidelines across Bolt Market and Bolt Food
#* At the moment the BM guidelines are that if the missing/wrong/expired/damaged item(s) is more than 50% of the order value, the eater is issued a *full refund*
#* The Bolt Food guidelines state that if there is an issue with one item, eater should be given Bolt Balance refund in the amount of that item + small compensation value, and if it’s 2+ items they get BB refund in the amount of those items + medium compensation value
#* Why should we unify the guidelines? Both BM and BF have *a similar user base*, the support experience should be as unified as possible. Also the *same CS agents* support both products, it would be easier for them to apply a unified, scalable process
#* Possible future steps:
#** Check (if possible) how many Bolt Market refunds were done per market per month & what % were full refunds (but this should include both full refunds to card & Bolt Balance refunds in the amount of the whole order value). 
#** Maybe we could test the Bolt Food guidelines on a few markets and see how it affects Bolt Market KPIs (including the probability of future orders) 
# The need (or lack thereof) for the local BM OPS-CS channels and the reports that CS agents post there
#* Currently it is expected that all reports of missing/wrong/damaged/expired items are reported manually by CS in the local BM OPS-CS channel
#* These channels were created in the early days of Bolt Market when there were more issues with supply and pickers, so it was decided that OPS should be made aware of every single issue with items the user received
#* We don’t have any insight into how closely this step is followed on all the markets, especially on the OPS side. If OPS are not doing anything with this information in real time & following up on every single case, there are better ways to get this data in bulk (deep-dives by ESC agents, Looker reports…) which would allow us to simplify these processes
#* Possible future steps: check with TLs/BM OPS managers how this information is used on a daily basis. If our doubts that OPS do not follow up on cases as they are reported are confirmed, we suggest switching to other kinds of reports mentioned above

{code:sql}with user_first_ride as (
select 
	user_id, 
	min(created) first_ride,
	count(*) ride_count
from carsharing.rental_car_order_order
where state = 'finished'
and created>'2022-03-17 13:00:00'
group by 1
),
doc_verification as (
select 
	user_id, 
	min(created) first_verification
from carsharing.rental_user_user_verification_state 
where created>'2022-03-17 13:00:00'
group by 1
),
successful_verification as (
select 
	user_id, 
	min(created) successful_verification
from carsharing.rental_user_user_verification_state 
where created>'2022-03-17 13:00:00'
and status in ('verified','verified_manually')
group by 1
)
select 
	treatment_id, 
	count(auth_id) enrolled, 
	count(case when first_verification is not null then first_verification else null end) started_verifying,
	count(case when successful_verification is not null then successful_verification else null end) succeeded_verification,
	count(case when first_ride is not null then first_ride else null end) made_at_least_1_ride,
	sum(ride_count) rides_done,
	100.0*started_verifying/enrolled as conversion_to_verification_attempt,
	100.0*succeeded_verification/enrolled as conversion_to_successful_verification,	
	100.0*made_at_least_1_ride/enrolled as conversion_to_first_ride,
	100.0*rides_done/enrolled as rides_per_user,
	100.0*rides_done/made_at_least_1_ride as rides_per_activated_user
from (
select 
    te.auth_id,
    te.treatment_id,
    ufr.first_ride,
    ufr.ride_count,
    dv.first_verification,
    sv.successful_verification
from public.targeting_enrollment te 
left join user_first_ride ufr on te.auth_id =ufr.user_id 
left join doc_verification dv on te.auth_id =dv.user_id 
left join successful_verification sv on te.auth_id =sv.user_id 
WHERE te.created>'2022-03-17 13:00:00'
    AND te.created< '2022-04-15 00:00:00'
	and te.treatment_id in (7608,7609,7610)
)

Hi Iva,

The regulatory risk surrounding Bolt Balance concerns the top-up function. The risk is that, because of the top-up function, Bolt Balance is deemed as an instrument for e-money and require that Bolt obtains a relevant license.

Currently, Bolt Balance is live with the top-up function only in the NL and BE. In all other jurisdictions the top-up function is available to Bolt employees only. 

In essence, having the top-up function available to Bolt employees is also subject to the risk of Bolt Balance being deemed as a payment instrument for e-money and require that Bolt obtains a relevant license. However, that risk is not deemed material. 

Best regards,

Sven

What is required:

An endpoint in *Admin Panel* (NOT on backend internal API), which will take {{source_id}} from booking, which currently is {{user_basket_auth_id}} (not {{order_id}}), and maybe some other parameters like {{city_id}}, {{user_id}} e.t.c., and *do a redirect* to an order page (also in Admin Panel). Endpoint url should be something like this:

{{https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/redirectToOrder/?user_basket_auth_id={{user_basket_auth_id}}&city_id={{city_id}}&user_id={{user_id}}}}

This means that this endpoint in Admin Panel will take these parameters, transform them to an order id and do a redirect to order page: {{https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/orders/{{order_id}}?cityId={{city_id}}}}



What this is for:

On our [Transaction History|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] page we need put a link from booking to order. We have a template in our config for every business line (like this {{https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-order/redirectToOrder/?source_id={{source_id}}&city_id={{city_id}}&user_id={{user_id}}}}) to which we substitute data from bookings to build a link for each booking. But for Delivery we don’t have {{order_id}} explicitly, we only have {{user_basket_auth_id}}, and we are also not going request {{order_id}} for each booking in the list, that’s why we need this endpoint. We will build a link by a template, and then this link will lead to you Admin Panel endpoint which in turn will redirect admin user to order page.

There is a good example for RidaHailing orders which does exactly the same.

{noformat}# MySQL EC2 metadata plugin

Exposes EC2 instance metadata using INFORMATION_SCHEMA.

## Disclaimer

mysql-ec2-metadata plugin can crash your server, corrupt your data, empty your credit card or burn down your neighbor's house, ... I don't take any responsibility for this !

## Description

MySQL EC2 metadata plugin downloads EC2 instance metadata from metadata service and exposes downloaded information in INFORMATION_SCHEMA.EC2_META table:

```mysql> select * from EC2_META;
+--------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------+
| METAOPT                        | VALUE                                         |
+--------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------+
| placement/availability-zone    | eu-central-1b                                 |
| placement/availability-zone-id | euc1-az3                                      |
| placement/region               | eu-central-1                                  |
| ami-id                         | ami-0a95c78892a8d8b50                         |
| ami-launch-index               | 0                                             |
| ami-manifest-path              | (unknown)                                     |
| hostname                       | ip-172-29-55-67.eu-central-1.compute.internal |
| instance-action                | none                                          |
| instance-id                    | i-0482dce76cd95cf93                           |
| instance-life-cycle            | on-demand                                     |
| instance-type                  | m6i.xlarge                                    |
| local-hostname                 | ip-172-29-55-67.eu-central-1.compute.internal |
| local-ipv4                     | 172.29.55.67                                  |
| mac                            | 06:ac:da:ec:90:00                             |
| profile                        | default-hvm                                   |
| reservation-id                 | r-09985cb3c47c494f3                           |
| security-groups                | default                                       |
+--------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------+
17 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```
EC2 metadata is only downloaded once when the EC2_META table is first read, usually this information does not change while the instance is running. To reload the data please use ```uninstall plugin``` and ```install plugin``` command or restart MySQL.

## Why ? Use cases
mysql-ec2-metadata plugin makes MySQL AWS EC2 aware. This helps to build smarter automation or tools needed for your MySQL database infrastructure.  The information exposed in the EC2_META table can be used in many different ways.

#### Integrating MySQL Orchestrator and mysql-ec2-metadata plugin:

This can be done in two simple steps:
* install mysql-ec2-metadata
* edit MySQL Orchestrator config, add:
```"DetectDataCenterQuery": "select VALUE from information_schema.ec2_meta where metaopt='placement/availability-zone';",```

![Orchestrator](https://github.com/TarmoKople/mysql-ec2-metadata/blob/main/images/orchestrator.png)

## Getting Started

### Dependencies

* MySQL

### Installing

mysql> INSTALL PLUGIN EC2_META SONAME 'ec2_meta.so';

### Executing program

mysql> SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.EC2_META;

### Uninstalling

mysql> UNINSTALL PLUGIN EC2_META;

## Building
### Preparing the environment
These instructions are for Ubuntu (20.04)
Setup build environment.
```
apt install build-essential
apt install pkg-config
```
Enable source repositories for your system. (edit /etc/apt/sources.list, uncomment lines starting with ```#deb-src``` and then run ```apt update```) 
Install dependencies needed to build MySQL:
```
apt build-dep mysql-server
```
Download and unpack MySQL source code:
```
apt source mysql-server
```
### Compiling the Plugin
This step is not Linux distribution specific. The same method can be used for any Linux distribution if the build environment is properly set up.
Enter to MySQL source directory
```
cd mysql-<version>
```

Download the plugin source code and store it under MySQL plugins directory. The easiest way is to use git. In MySQL source directory do:
```
git clone https://github.com/TarmoKople/mysql-ec2-metadata.git plugin/ec2-metadata
```
This downloads source code to plugins/ec2-metadata directory.
* **NB!** if you need source code for MySQL 5.7 please check out **5.7** branch

Create a build directory (builddir) inside MySQL source directory, cd to builddir and configure the source
```
mkdir builddir
cd builddir
cmake -DDOWNLOAD_BOOST=1 -DWITH_BOOST=. ..
```

To build the plugin and MySQL type ```make``` in builddir, to build just the plugin ```make ec2_meta```

Compiled plugin can be found under: builddir/plugin_output_directory/ec2_meta.so

#### Installing compiled plugin
Copy compiled plugin to MySQL plugin directory. To find out where is the plugin directory is located execute:
```
mysql> SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE "%plugin_dir%";
+---------------+-------------------------+
| Variable_name | Value                   |
+---------------+-------------------------+
| plugin_dir    | /usr/lib/mysql/plugin/  |
+---------------+-------------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

For Ubuntu / Debian it is by default /usr/lib/mysql/plugin
```
cp plugin_output_directory/ec2_meta.so /usr/lib/mysql/plugin/
```

Hi Julian, you are correct, we would need more info to assess the request. I’ll include some points below, but in general I think we are missing the context of the investigation + the fact that we can’t actually find any info with the details provided to proceed. 

* Email address ends in the local authorities official address
* The identity and authority of the officer is confirmed (look for certain identifying marks such as officers name, badge number etc.) 
* E-mail includes a disclosure request as an attachment.
* Has an official law enforcement agency's letterhead. The letterhead has certain identifying marks such as signature and stamp by the appropriate officer who is empowered by local law to represent the law enforcement agency
* Make sure the personal data is requested in connection with alleged crime (there is context and some details given of the investigation in hand): 
** Case number, investigators name and contact information
** Specific trip info (e.g date, time range, pick up or drop off location, vehicle licence plate number)
** Or all known email addresses, names, and phone numbers of the user(s) whose personal data is requested
* Precise description of information requested, reasoning of why information is requested, and how it pertains to investigation of the alleged crime
* Reference to applicable provisions of the relevant law (e.g domestic Data Protection Act) under which the agency is entitled to request the information. 
* Cites a provision for disclosure

Hey [~accountid:5fc8dff0aca10c0069d470f1] and [~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e], jumping in here to elaborate a bit on Bolt Balance feature.

There are separate T&Cs for Bolt Balance (please see [here|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/2lgOlpDbGaWFvEtbOhBL5u/12150c515cc7f445e11a23fe816619d2/Bolt_Balance_Terms_and_Conditions__effective_as_of_31_March_2022_.pdf]). +Please note that according to my understanding Bolt Balance has not been launched in Malta yet+. Please refer to the expansion plan for Bolt Balance [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3717300667/Balance+expansion+plan+2022].

Section 1.1.2 of the T&Cs stipulates that amount on Bolt Balance may also be accrued as a result of us making refunds to Bolt Balance. This does not, however, mean that the Bolt Balance T&Cs would give us the contractual right to do refunds / compensation exclusively to Bolt Balance and even if they did, then this does not mean that applicable laws would not override such contractual right and allow us to do refunds / compensation exclusively to Bolt Balance. Most likely, applicable laws should be understood so as to leave users with the right to demand that refunds / compensation in cash no matter what we write in our T&Cs - i.e. by way of making a transfer to the user’s bank account or by rescinding a card payment.

With regard to partial refunds, the only compliant way to do this is to ask user for his/her consent before doing the partial refund to Bolt Balance. We cannot add consent of the user to our T&Cs by default. However, since the amount of complaints is likely not high and we are not talking about high amounts, then it might be worth taking a risk to make partial refunds without having express consent of the user. This is, however, a business decision that should be discussed with Bolt Balance team.

[~accountid:5de0e80a2c5dd20d0f8ffb6a] Hey, do you know if these are questions you have asked them already before going on holiday?

*On the legality of BB not being transferable to another currency*

A section on this has been added to the Bolt Balance T&Cs (Section 1.7). 

Applicable laws will probably not be sufficiently clear on whether this is a term which would ultimately be valid and enforceable vis-a-vis consumers. In my opinion, this limitation should be deemed valid and enforceable under relevant EU level consumer protection directives (Consumer Rights Directive and Distance Marketing Directive) and under relevant EE laws for that matter. But other local laws and consumer protection authorities may take another view. 

I think it is one of those questions, where we might want to take an aggressive approach and go with it, accepting the fact that consumers may rightfully raise this as an issue and being prepared to redeem these amounts to users by bank transfer to the user’s account where amounts are significant and the user adamant. But this is both a legal and a business decision. Not sure whether we can get full legal clarity on this. So we might need to accept some risk and take an approach. Trusting the legal end of this with @epp.aasaru.

*On whether we should avoid doing BB refunds if a user is from another country*

I think we should, yes. 

Otherwise we might end up with a lot of users who never get to use that refund we give them. If someone relocates from one country / currency to another then what use does he / she have of amounts which he / she can use when those amounts would only be usable if he / she should ever return to where he / she is from.

* *_also tell the user if they don’t respond back in 5 (?) days we will delete the account._*
* *_if no response, delete account._*

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] , I finally received the SK response regarding this matter. 

As we both assumed, it is similar to any other national legislation.

Please find below their answer. And should you have any questions, please let me know\! 

P.S. Happy birthday once again\!\!\!\! :)))

+*Answer Slovakia*+ 

“Having a chance to analyse this matter, please find below our legal views. As the return process depends on the regulation of rights and obligations related to delivery of the goods, we elaborate on the point 2. Stock acceptance first and later we continue with the next points.

# *Stock acceptance*

If not specifically agreed otherwise, the Slovak law requires that buyer checks the goods and claims deficient goods with the supplier _without undue delay after their delivery_. A written agreement can adjust the period for the check of the goods though, and therefore set a broader/more specific period, within which the buyer is entitled to exercise its right to claim damaged goods.

The extracted provision from the supplier contracts regulates the matter fairly. We only suggest minor adjustments to the wording, so that it clearly states that Bolt is not only entitled to raise the claims, but is also entitled to perform the check of the goods within the 24-hour period. Please see below:

_’Bolt has no obligation to check the goods delivered by supplier_ *_immediately_* _upon delivery. Acceptance of goods upon delivery shall in no way be considered as a waiver of claims regarding the quality or quantity of the goods. Bolt is entitled to check the delivered goods and raise claims regarding deficient goods to the supplier within 24 hours after the delivery of the goods.’_

As to the delivery notes, we confirm that it is sufficient and protects Bolt from its liability too. We do suggest a single minor adjustments so that it reflects the suggested agreement’s provision. This also prevents from an interpretation of the statement which might indicate that Bolt has not checked the goods at all. Please see below:

_‘With this delivery note the supplier acknowledges that_ *_immediately_* _upon delivery Bolt has not inspected the quality, quantity, the packaging, the expiration date nor the health and safety of the delivered goods.’_

As long as the written supply agreement clearly provides Bolt a 24-hour period to check and claim deficient goods (moreover, if this is accompanied with the delivery note statement), we opine that there is no need for any other means to prevent potential negative outcomes of not checking the goods immediately upon the delivery. 

# *Return process*

We confirm that the described return process is sufficient and there are no legal obstacles for using it under the Slovak legislation. The suggested list of documents is also satisfactory and the legislation does not require to procure any further documentation.

Unfortunately, the Slovak legislation is not clear about the validity of delivery of such documents by e-mail communication, if not specifically agreed by parties. Therefore, we advise to do one of the following:

# Incorporate a provision into the supply agreement by which the parties expressly agree to delivery of any/certain correspondence by e-mail; or
Execute the documents in a form of a signed paper version.

It is not required to have a signed document proving the return of the goods by the supplier. We though strongly advise to have a proof of their delivery anyways (p. e. a delivery receipt from a transport service company), to protect Bolt in case of any disputes.

# *Storage of delivery notes*

 Originals of delivery notes should be stored and should be easily accessible in the case of an inspection by public authorities, p. e. Tax Office. Even though it is not specifically required by law, the inspection authorities always prefer to be provided with originals of such documents and might not accept their scanned versions, especially if the inspected matter/relevant delivery of goods is disputable in any way.

As the delivery notes are a part of Bolt’s accounting files, the Act no. 431/2002 Coll on Accounting requires they are stored for *ten years* following the year in which they were issued.”



BR, 

Iva

*After the investigation*: the problem with the full address is actual only for active order flow and for the rides history, all other cases of full addresses in the interfaces were bugs that are already fixed.

*The reason:* we show in the interface exactly the address we pass in createRide/createScheduledRide request. 

*Why we need to pass full address (with the index) in this request right now:* because we show exactly this string in driver app and we need to show full address to the drivers to avoid the confusion.

*The problem is deeper than only indexes*: because we show the exact string from the rider app in driver app and because rider and driver can have different languages selected in their app, we can show drivers the address in the language they don’t expect or understand. 

*The proposed solution*: to separate the addresses we show in rider app and driver app. We provide coordinates and place id to the backend in createRide/createScheduledRide. That’s enough to identify the place for both rider and driver, address is not required. We’ll continue sending this data and backend will do reverse geocoding for the coordinates on its side and send to the driver the correct full address in the language selected in driver’s app. 

*To achieve the proposed solution we need to do:*

#  to switch to the flow with additional reverse geocoding on the backend; 
# to start sending address instead of full address in createRide/createScheduledRide on clients (estimation is 0.25 for both ios and android).

Since we’re talking about assumption of potentially significant legal risk and resulting financial exposure, we have 2 options:

(1) Option 1: You reach out to the INFOBIP and explain that the wording of the indemnity is too broad and we would like to at least cap the maximum liability amount before signing the letter (the agreed amount can be determined by you - what seems reasonable in the context of potential exposure to both parties).
